headline: High-risk shared-write coding pair: broad filesystem, git, network, and MCP access create prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write files, use MCP, and operate on shared work artifacts. Devin’s shared_state_with_other_instances via integrations and Gemini CLI’s shared_state via filesystem/git create a plausible instruction-bridging path if one agent consumes the other’s outputs as trusted content. This is not proven by docs to be automatic, so medium fits.
conditions: IF either agent reads the other agent’s generated files as instructions without provenance checks
IF both agents are pointed at the same repo or cwd
IF MCP tools expose attacker-controlled content to either agent
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic ingestion of peer-generated files
Add provenance tags to shared artifacts
Restrict MCP servers to allowlisted, read-only sources
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin handles repo deploy keys and integration tokens and can write to Slack/Linear/Jira/Notion, while Gemini CLI reads repo files and user-provided directories and sends context to Google APIs. If both touch the same workspace, sensitive code or secrets can flow from Devin’s cloud workspace into Gemini’s outbound context, creating a realistic exfiltration path in default setups.
conditions: IF both agents access the same repository or directory
IF secrets are present in files or environment variables visible to Gemini CLI
IF Devin’s workspace contents are copied into Gemini CLI prompts or tool context
mitigations: Remove secrets from shared directories
Use separate repos or clones per agent
Rotate any exposed tokens immediately
Disable outbound API access for the agent handling sensitive files
requires-engineering: enforce secret redaction before cross-agent handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, package installation, and git-state modification. Devin’s cloud workspace and Gemini CLI’s default user-level execution can both mutate the same repo or cwd, and Gemini explicitly shares state via filesystem and git only. Without locking, concurrent writes and git races are a high-probability conflict.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git branch or working tree
IF either agent auto-commits or rewrites files while the other is active
IF no external lock or merge gate is enforced
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent
Use a file or git lock before edits
Require manual merge review
Pause one agent during the other’s write phase
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor, and Gemini CLI is a tool-using terminal agent that can act on files and shell output. If Gemini consumes Devin’s outputs as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into edits, commits, or external actions. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, so the safer high severity is warranted.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI uses Devin-produced text as task instructions or facts
IF Devin’s outputs are forwarded into shell commands, commits, or tickets without review
IF no human verification step is inserted between agents
mitigations: Insert a human review gate
Require structured handoff templates
Compare outputs against source files before acting
Limit Gemini to read-only verification on Devin outputs
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking and diff validation

E_compliance.rationale: Devin’s docs show Slack, Linear, Jira, and Notion write scopes plus cloud workspace files, while Gemini CLI sends prompts to Google’s generative API and reads user directories. If regulated or sensitive data is placed in the shared workspace, retention and residency obligations may diverge across vendors. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace
IF organizational policy forbids sending that data to external model APIs
IF retention or deletion requirements differ across Slack, Jira, Notion, Google, or workspace storage
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Use separate tenants for sensitive projects
Review vendor retention settings
Disable writes to collaboration tools for sensitive tasks
requires-engineering: perform a formal data-flow and DPA review
